blocks.text: Condo buildings in Greentree Village

The City of Burnaby's own Greentree Community Plan (1972) describes the Greentree site as a 50-acre site bounded by Wayburne Drive to the west, Woodsworth Street to the north, Forest Lawn Cemetery to the east and Moscrop Street to the south — the same V5G pocket, not Marlborough/Sussex.
Streets, schools and getting around Greentree Village

items.t: The City's 1972 Greentree Community Plan bounds the original Greentree site by Wayburne Drive (west), Woodsworth Street (north), Forest Lawn Cemetery (east) and Moscrop Street (south). Exact MLS sub-area boundary streets beyond that plan area are not verified — the City publishes no street-by-street written boundary for the MLS sub-area.

Where the condo stock actually concentrates: there is no verified apartment-condo building in the sub-area. The named stock is the Greentree Village townhouse village itself — multiple strata phases, all named "Greentree Village," spread across the Garden Grove / Fernglen / Cedarglen street cluster — ringed by detached houses. SnapStats publishes the sub-area's attached figures as "Condos & Townhomes" combined, so the figures cannot separate the townhome share.

Burnaby community level (SnapStats publishes medians at community level only): Condos & Townhomes median sale price $686,000, $763/sqft, sale-to-list 98%, 36 days on market in September 2026. No Greentree Village sub-area median exists.

Transit and roads for the verified pocket: Canada Way and Highway 1 run along the north side, Willingdon Avenue / BCIT to the west, Deer Lake Park to the east. A SkyTrain station inside the pocket: none verified.

Anchors for the verified pocket: Greentree Village Park / playground beside the Fernglen townhomes, the Greentree recreation facility across from the Garden Grove townhomes (indoor pool, fitness centre and social room per a listing source), Deer Lake Park and trails, and BCIT.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect condo buyers in Greentree Village

items.t: City plans and zoning (Burnaby): the current Burnaby Zoning Bylaw is the Zoning Bylaw 2026 (No. 14815, adopted June 9, 2026, in effect July 1, 2026); the former Zoning Bylaw 1965 (No. 4742) is repealed — do not cite it as current. The Burnaby 2050 Official Community Plan, adopted December 9, 2025, replaces the 1998 OCP and takes precedence over older community-plan maps where they conflict, and the City's R1 Small-Scale Multi-Unit Housing district (from June 2024) lets surrounding house lots hold 3 units on lots up to 280 m², 4 units on larger lots, and 6 units on lots of at least 281 m² within 400 m of a frequent-transit stop — that SSMUH permission applies to the freehold house lots around the village, not to the strata townhouse parcels themselves.

Burnaby tax timing: City of Burnaby property taxes for 2026 were due Friday, July 3, 2026; a 5% penalty applies to outstanding current taxes after the July due date and a further 5% after the September due date.

blocks.text: Good to know about Greentree Village

items.t: Its Marlborough/Sussex/Metrotown location, its École Marlborough and Burnaby South school discussion, and its Royal Oak transit anchor all belong to a different pocket; the City's own 1972 Greentree Community Plan and every Greentree Village-classified listing place the sub-area south of Canada Way behind BCIT.

The village predates its own community plan's build-out era and is still one name across many stratas. The City plan for the 50-acre Greentree site dates to November 6, 1972 (Manager's Report No. 72, Rezoning #1/72), planned at roughly 450 units at 12 units/acre — the phases that listings now date to 1974–1975 are that plan being built, which is why one name covers multiple separate strata corporations.

Burnaby's zoning bylaw changed under this stock mid-2026. The Zoning Bylaw 2026 (No. 14815) was adopted June 9, 2026 and took effect July 1, 2026, replacing the repealed 1965 Bylaw No. 4742, and the Burnaby 2050 OCP (adopted December 9, 2025) replaced the 1998 OCP — a Greentree document or listing citing the old bylaw numbers is citing repealed law.
The whole sub-area can have a three-listing month.

The houses around the townhomes now carry multiplex value the townhomes do not. Under Burnaby's R1 SSMUH district, surrounding freehold lots can hold 3–4 homes (6 near frequent transit) and lots with two or more primary units may be stratified — the detached streets around the village price partly on that permission, while the strata parcels' value stays in the existing townhome form.
A "Phase IV" exists in the village's own naming.

items.t: "Greentree Village" is the GVR board sub-area name as used in the SnapStats GVR report for Burnaby, and the name of the planned community in the City's Greentree Village Community Plan (Manager's Report No. 72, Rezoning #1/72, dated November 6, 1972): a roughly 50-acre site south of Canada Way and Highway 1, behind BCIT and west of Deer Lake, bounded by Wayburne Drive (W), Woodsworth Street (N), Forest Lawn Cemetery (E) and Moscrop Street (S), planned for about 450 units at 12 units per acre. The village streets are Garden Grove Drive, Fernglen Drive/Place, Cedarglen Place, Laurelwood Place, Elmgrove Drive, Driftwood Place and Village Drive.
Where the townhouse stock concentrates: the whole village — it is a townhouse village built in strata phases, surrounded by detached streets.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect townhome buyers in Greentree Village

items.t: Form B diligence (each counted phase — separately): Strata Property Act s. 59 — the Form B states the lot's monthly strata fees, amounts owing, approved special levies still payable, the CRF balance and an insurance summary, with the rules, current budget, any Rental Disclosure Statement and the most recent depreciation report attached; provided within 7 days, maximum $35 plus up to 25 cents per page. Because each Greentree phase is its own strata corporation, a Form B from one phase says nothing about any other phase — order the package for the phase the unit actually sits in, identified by civic address and strata plan, not by the village name.

blocks.text: Good to know about Greentree Village

items.t: Greentree Village is older than the SkyTrain, older than BCIT's current campus form, and older than most of Burnaby's townhouse stock: it was planned in a single City report dated November 6, 1972 (Manager's Report No. 72, Rezoning #1/72) at about 450 units on roughly 50 acres — a complete townhouse village approved before "townhouse" was a common Burnaby form.

The village's east boundary is a cemetery: Forest Lawn Cemetery closes the site on the east, which is why the village's streets are all internal crescents and places with no through traffic — and why Deer Lake trails, not roads, continue east.
A "100% sales ratio" for this sub-area in September 2026 means two listings sold out of two listings. With stock this thin, sub-area statistics here describe individual sales, not a market.

blocks.text: Lots and land in Greentree Village
The one named land development

items.t: Greentree Village (City of Burnaby Greentree Village Community Plan, Manager's Report No. 72, Rezoning #1/72, dated Nov 6, 1972): a roughly 50-acre planned site south of Canada Way behind BCIT, bounded by Wayburne Drive (W), Woodsworth Street (N), Forest Lawn Cemetery (E) and Moscrop Street (S), planned for about 450 units at 12 units per acre. That 1972 plan is the subdivision document for this ground: the village streets (Garden Grove Drive, Fernglen Drive/Place, Cedarglen Place, Laurelwood Place, Elmgrove Drive, Driftwood Place, Village Drive) are its built fabric, not a current lot offering, and no lot sizes, lot counts for sale, or prices are stated — none exists as an offering. Servicing as the plan/source states it: no parcel-level servicing statement for the village is quoted in the sources read — City water/sewer position for a specific parcel: confirm with the City.

How the plan was built out (cross-reference only, no recount): the village was delivered as multiple strata townhouse phases, each phase its own strata corporation. Detached houses also sit on village streets; they are single-family homes, not a land offering.

blocks.text: Fee-simple lots

items.t: Surrounding and in-village detached lots: fee-simple single-family houses ring the strata phases and sit on some village streets — the freehold side of the pocket.

Servicing, as the City states it (city-wide frame): Burnaby's 2026 residential utility notice covers annual water, annual sewer use, a cross-connection device charge where applicable, and a residential garbage toter fee; the detached single-family dwelling water charge is $652.33, rates carry a 5% discount if paid by the due date, and for single-family homes sewer is billed as a sewer parcel tax on the property tax notice. Parcel-level servicing for a specific lot: confirm with the City.
ALR vs non-ALR: no ALR split is documented for this pocket, and no ALR percentage is stated. Parcel-level ALR status is checked in the Agricultural Land Commission's ALR Property and Map Finder.

Hazard position, corrected pocket: For the corrected Canada Way / Deer Lake pocket, parcel-level hazard and streamside status (Deer Lake edge) is a property-specific check: Not verified for individual lots.

items.t: No bare-land strata plan in Greentree Village was verified: The village's strata phases are building strata (townhouses on strata lots within a built complex), which is a different form from a bare-land strata subdivision.

items.t: Greentree Village, on the corrected geography followed here, is a small planned pocket in the City of Burnaby south of Canada Way and Highway 1, behind BCIT and west of Deer Lake: a roughly 50-acre site bounded by Wayburne Drive (W), Woodsworth Street (N), Forest Lawn Cemetery (E) and Moscrop Street (S), planned in 1972 for about 450 units at 12 units per acre. The village streets are Garden Grove Drive, Fernglen Drive/Place, Cedarglen Place, Laurelwood Place, Elmgrove Drive, Driftwood Place and Village Drive. "Greentree Village" is the GVR board sub-area name in the SnapStats GVR September 2026 report under community "Burnaby." City use of "Greentree Village" as an official neighbourhood name beyond its 1972 community plan was not confirmed.
Roads and transit, corrected pocket: Canada Way is the arterial along the pocket's north side. Commute times in minutes: Not verified.
Schools, corrected pocket: SD41 (Burnaby) operates 41 elementary and 8 secondary schools city-wide, with no middle-school tier — elementary K–7, secondary 8–12.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Greentree Village

items.t: SSMUH / subdivision potential as the City states it (surrounding fee-simple house lots only, NOT the strata townhouse parcels): R1 lots may hold 3 units on lots up to 280 m², 4 units on larger lots, and 6 units on lots of at least 281 m² within 400 m of a frequent-transit stop; lots with two or more primary units may be stratified; SSMUH lots require a minimum lot width of 10 m and a minimum lot area of 281 m²; permitted forms include single-family homes, duplexes, multiplexes, rowhouses and secondary suites.

Strata block (applies to the village's building-strata phases; no bare-land strata is verified here): Form B diligence (provided within 7 days, max $35 + 25¢/page) — each Greentree phase is its own strata corporation with its own Form B, CRF and depreciation report; depreciation reports on a 5-year cycle for stratas with 5+ lots since July 1, 2024; minimum 10% CRF contribution since November 1, 2023; rental-restriction bylaws VOID since November 24, 2022 (short-term restrictions may still apply by bylaw); only 55+ age bylaws valid under SPA ss.123.1/123.2, with May 1, 2023 exemptions; a listing's "45+" line is NOT a valid BC age bylaw.

ALR rules (for completeness — no Greentree Village ALR parcel is confirmed here): subdivision within the ALR requires ALC approval; ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s. 6; SPA s. 239; ALCA s. 21(1)); ALC residence caps: principal ≤500 m², suite within principal only, additional residence 90 m² (≤40 ha) / 186 m² (>40 ha).

The City's 1972 Greentree Community Plan bounds the original site by Wayburne Drive, Woodsworth Street, Forest Lawn Cemetery and Moscrop Street.

None verified. The named strata stock is the Greentree Village townhouse village in several same-named phases; the surrounding stock is detached houses. SnapStats' "Condos & Townhomes" category for the sub-area combines the two forms and does not change that.
faq.q: Are there any apartment condos in Greentree Village?

faq.a: That reading is a tiny-sample artefact: the sub-area had exactly 2 condos & townhomes listings that month and both sold. Price off a multi-month window and Garden Village / Deer Lake / Burnaby-wide comparables (Burnaby Condos & Townhomes median $686,000 in September 2026), not off one 2-listing month.
faq.q: Everything sold in September 2026 — is this a hot market?

faq.a: Because each phase is a separate strata corporation with its own bylaws, CRF, depreciation report and levies, while sharing the "Greentree Village" name and the recreation amenities listings describe. The strata plan number for the specific phase is not confirmed from usable sources (the only directory found was not usable) — get it from title and order that phase's documents, not another phase's.
faq.q: One complex name, several phases — why does it matter?

faq.a: 1970s, per the usable listings: Fernglen Place units stated built 1974, Garden Grove and Cedarglen units stated built 1975. One conflict: an older feature sheet for 4328 Garden Grove Drive stated 1997 where the current listing states 1975 — not confirmed for that unit; verify the phase's year on the strata plan.

In the V5G pocket south of Canada Way behind BCIT, at the west edge of Deer Lake — bounded by Wayburne Drive, Woodsworth Street, Forest Lawn Cemetery and Moscrop Street under the City's 1972 Greentree Village Community Plan.
No verified one — the village is completed 1970s stock: strata townhouse phases plus detached houses on village streets. No lot offering, bare-land strata or presale lot sale was verified.

faq.a: A bare-land strata (owning a lot inside a strata plan) is a different form, and none was verified here.

Where is Greentree Village in Burnaby?
faq.a: On Burnaby's south slope around Marlborough Avenue and Sussex Avenue, near École Marlborough Elementary, west of Metrotown; "Greentree Village" is the GVR MLS® sub-area name, matching the local townhome pocket (SnapStats, September 2026)

faq.a: École Marlborough Elementary (K–7), 6060 Marlborough Ave — a French Immersion program school; Immersion entry is application-based, and the catchment for any specific address must be checked in the SD41 School Locator.
